clue.text: Had spread rumour about attachment

indicators.note: spread here means scattered around, so the three letters of the first word are rearranged
about means turned round, so the word for rumour is read backwards

parts.note: rumour is noise, as in talk going around

explanation.surface: Someone spread gossip about a person's romantic attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges HAD to ADH; 'about' turns NOISE into ESION.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical sticking together of two surfaces is a kind of attachment, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Consents but will be a long time coming round again

indicators.note: coming round means surrounding, so the long-time word goes round the other piece

parts.note: ages means a long time
RE is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, but only after a long wait for the next occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to give assent, so consents and agrees are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Is jesting about providing support in flight

indicators.note: about means around, so the jesting word surrounds the opening word

parts.note: jesting is banter, playful teasing talk

explanation.surface: Joking around while giving support during an aeroplane flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not air travel; 'Is' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A handrail running up a staircase supports people climbing a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Plant the Italian found in rock climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
found in means placed inside the rock word

parts.note: a crag is a steep rock
IL is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: A plant spotted growing in the rock during an Italian climbing trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts IL into CRAG as CILRAG; 'climbing' reverses that whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulb of this strong-smelling allium is a common cooking plant.

clue.text: Scoundrel best avoided by soldiers

parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg, and a rotten one is best avoided; also a rogue that army men should shun

explanation.surface: Troops should steer clear of a rotten character.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'soldiers' are fingers of toast for dipping into soft-boiled eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a dishonest or unpleasant person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Writer to ring firm up

parts.note: to ring is to bell, sound a bell

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A writer phones a company to set it going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CO into OC. Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French writer of cautionary verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc was a poet and essayist, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Scholar regrettably about to make obeisance

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A regretful scholar is about to bow down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' but turns MAALAS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To salaam is to bow low with the hand on the forehead, a gesture of obeisance.

clue.text: Revolutionary form of Taoism

indicators.note: form of means a new shape of the letters, so the religion's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A radical version of an ancient Chinese philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Mao Zedong's communist doctrine is a revolutionary.

clue.text: A spokesman?

parts.note: read literally, a man who makes spokes, as for cartwheels, rather than someone speaking for others

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks on behalf of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who builds wooden wheels fits the spokes into them.

clue.text: Maintain there's some body in the beer

indicators.note: in means placed inside the beer word

parts.note: ale is beer
a leg is one part of a body

explanation.surface: Claiming there is something solid floating in one's pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some body' reads as a person but means one part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or claim, which is one sense of maintain.

clue.text: Textile manufacturer's bequest to his son?

definitions.text: Textile manufacturer's bequest to his son?

parts.words: Textile manufacturer's bequest to his son?
parts.note: a weaver's machine left to his successor: the successor plus the weaving frame

explanation.surface: A mill owner leaves something to his boy in his will.
explanation.definitionFit: A valued item handed down through generations of a family is a bequest of this kind.

clue.text: Baked beans need this lid for protection

definitions.text: Baked beans need this lid for protection

parts.words: Baked beans need this lid for protection
parts.note: bean is slang for head, so sunbaked heads need a hat to shield them

explanation.surface: A cook covers a tin of baked beans.
explanation.walkthrough: A topi is a sun helmet; 'lid' is slang for a hat and 'bean' for a head.
explanation.definitionFit: This lightweight pith helmet shields the head from the sun, hence a protective lid.

clue.text: A certain reluctance to give credit

definitions.text: A certain reluctance to give credit

parts.words: A certain reluctance to give credit
parts.note: not lending money, as it seems, but being unwilling to believe what one is told

explanation.surface: A bank is wary of lending.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubt and disbelief mean refusing to give credence, which is credit in its believing sense.

clue.text: Southern way out unfit for the voyage

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The southern route is ruled out as unsuitable for sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel not safe to put to sea is unfit to make a voyage.

clue.text: One sort of examiner always circles a wrong mark

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so the always word goes round the mark

parts.note: eternal means lasting for ever, always
X is the mark for a wrong answer

explanation.surface: An examiner keeps circling incorrect answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' puts X inside ETERNAL. An external examiner checks marking from outside the institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities appoint an outside assessor, called an external, to check exam standards.

clue.text: Distributes striking proclamation

definitions.meaning: a call for workers to down tools and come out on strike

explanation.definitionFit: To hand things round is to distribute; a strike call announces workers' hands are out.

clue.text: Put off by girl wanting affection but no ring

parts.note: she refers to a girl

indicators.note: but no means without, so the ring letter is removed

parts.note: love is affection
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A man is put off by a girl lacking warmth and refusing an engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no' takes O from LOVE, leaving LVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone it, to put it off for later.

clue.text: It takes an age to get a suntan

definitions.text: It takes an age to get a suntan

parts.words: It takes an age to get a suntan
parts.note: a long sunbathe gives a tanned colour, and the colour also names a prehistoric age

explanation.surface: Sunbathing for a tan takes forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bronze Age is a prehistoric period; bronze is also a tanned skin colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep tan gives a metallic brown colour, and that metal names an age.

clue.text: Austerity budget afoot

parts.note: a very tight budget, and literally a lace found on the foot

explanation.surface: A government cutback budget is in the offing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' seems to mean 'under way', but points to a lace worn on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny budget is said to be run on a lace, which is also worn on footwear.

clue.text: Numbers set out in rows

definitions.meaning: figures, as in the digit after seven
crews that go rowing, boats with eight oarsmen

explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a number, and rowing boats crewed by eight oarsmen are called this.

clue.text: Free a deserter held by soldiers

indicators.note: held by means contained inside the soldiers word

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts their side

explanation.surface: A deserter caught by troops is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: GIs is the usual crossword term for American soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given gratis is provided without charge, so it is free.

clue.text: Mean? No, jolly!

parts.note: taken as written
jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for being stingy instead of cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like miserly and 'jolly' like cheerful; mean is the average and a jolly is a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistical average or standard level is both a mean and the usual value.

clue.text: A boss in a limited company

definitions.text: A boss in a limited company

parts.words: A boss in a limited company
parts.note: not a business director but a ruler among a small group holding power

explanation.surface: A director of a limited liability firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a ruling clique, power held by a few, which is a limited company of bosses.

clue.text: Missing sailors — ten adrift

parts.note: ABs are able-bodied seamen, sailors

indicators.note: adrift means out of position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten crew members are lost at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present is missing, so absent is a synonym.

clue.text: Catch ten out with a quick blow

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the number's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rap is a quick sharp knock

explanation.surface: A batsman is caught out after a sharp hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap or ensnare someone is to catch them.

clue.text: Forms issued when there's no employment

indicators.note: forms here is a verb meaning makes into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Official forms are handed out to the unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' looks like paperwork but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of not being used, the absence of employment in its using sense.
